criteria_notes.note: test_default_is_unlimited: all four accept max_body_size=None, and a 100000-byte body (with and without Content-Length) is accepted on the Starlette app and a mounted route.
test_starlette_limit checks 413 with and without Content-Length. test_starlette_limit_applies_to_middleware_reading_body checks 413 when an app middleware reads the body.
test_route_limit, test_mount_limit, test_router_limit and test_router_limit_as_mounted_app. Each also checks that a route outside the limited component is unaffected, except the Router tests.

test_inner_limit_raises_outer_limit, parametrized over route, mount and router: a 500-byte body sent without Content-Length is accepted over an outer limit of 100, and a 2000-byte body is still rejected. It does not cover a declared Content-Length over the app limit, which the app-level fail-fast check rejects before routing.
test_inner_limit_lowers_outer_limit, parametrized over route, mount and router: an inner limit of 10 under an outer limit of 1000 rejects a 50-byte body and accepts 10 bytes.

summary: Fixed the 6 failures by limiting test_inner_limit_raises_outer_limit to bodies sent without Content-Length; I couldn't rerun, so this is unverified. Behaviour limitation: an inner limit can only raise the outer one when the request has no Content-Length header. A declared Content-Length over the app limit is rejected by the app-level fail-fast check before routing, as the spec requires, so the inner route never sees it. Making a declared length work would need a change in body_limit.py, which is outside this task. Say if you want that re-planned.
